newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle futures close lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle futures close lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower on pressure from growing cash concerns and profit taking, traders said.
Concern over topping action in choice boxed beef values and reluctance by packers to raise bids for fed cattle above $72 per cwt continued to weigh on the live cattle futures market, they said.
"There was disappointment (packers) havn't paid up for cash," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc.
Clarkson also cited a very weak technical picture in December and February contracts.

Expectations of increased fed cattle supplies late this year and into the next due to stepped up placements had been weighing on December and February most of the week. Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report is expected to bear this out.

Early projections on Friday's report for on-feed cattle supplies as of September 1 in the seven key states ranged from from 88.2 to 92 percent of a year ago, with the number of cattle placed in feedlots seen at 106.6 to 119 percent and marketings at 92 to 98 percent of a year ago.
Technical sell stops were also touched off on the setback before late short covering pared losses, they added.
Smith Barney sold October late into sell stops before RBH and Refco bought at the close. R.J. O'Brien and Cargill Investor Services notably sold December on the setback, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, February premium was up 1-1/2 percent as Merrill Lynch bought 62 to 64 puts and 70 to 72 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures continued to follow the lead of deferred live cattle contracts and fell to new day's lows late on sell stops. Increasing on-feed cattle supplies will reduce demand for replacement feeders, traders said.
They noted that pressure came despite lower corn futures and the highest price level for the feeder cattle index since December 27. Latest CME index was up $0.01 at $64.09 per cwt.

Chicago Corp, Prudential Securities and Stone Traders sold October late. There was long February live cattle/short October feeders and long May feeders/short October 1997 live cattle spreading, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.350 cent lower to unchanged with October off 0.175 at 72.825 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.150 to 0.750 lower with October off most at 64.175 cents.
